title: Kan-fibration slice models the coherent slice of spaces
statement:
Fix nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, coherent functors and mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the simplicial-category and coherent-nerve conventions of [def-coef-coherent-nerve-infrastructure], and $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal U})$ from [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $B$ be a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex. A Kan fibration means a simplicial map having the right lifting property against all horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$. Define the simplicial category $\mathcal K_B$ to have as objects all Kan fibrations $a:A\to B$ with $\mathcal U$-small total space and as mapping simplicial sets
$$\mathcal K_B(a,c)=\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)}\{a\},\qquad c:C\to B,$$
where the first map is postcomposition with $c$, the vertex $a$ is regarded as a constant simplicial map from $\Delta^0$, and composition and identities are inherited from simplicial maps. Let $P:\mathcal K_B\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ be the total-space functor, and let $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U,/B}$ be the coherent slice with its source projection $p_B$, in either of the equivalent join-slice and fixed-target-arrow models of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence]. Then $\mathcal K_B$ is locally Kan and there is a coherent functor
$$J:N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal K_B\longrightarrow\mathcal S_{\mathcal U,/B}$$
which sends $a:A\to B$ to the corresponding arrow of spaces, is fully faithful and essentially surjective, and has a coherent natural equivalence $p_BJ\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}P$. On mapping spaces the comparison induced by $J$ identifies the displayed strict fiber with
$$\operatorname{hofib}_{a}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}(A,C)\xrightarrow{c\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}(A,B)\bigr),$$
compatibly with the total-space projections, identities and coherent compositions. All categories are formed in a containing universe; the total spaces in $\mathcal K_B$ remain $\mathcal U$-small. Empty bases, total spaces and fibers are allowed.

source.place: Kerodon Example 5.5.1.23 (Tag 05Q0), using the slice dual of Proposition 5.5.1.22 (Tag 01ZT): full faithfulness, essential surjectivity by small fibration replacement, and the source-compatible mapping-fiber comparison. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For a Kan fibration $c:C\to B$ and any small simplicial set $A$, postcomposition $f:\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)$ is a Kan fibration. Indeed a horn problem transposes to a problem for $c$ against $A\times\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow A\times\Delta^m$. Apply [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow A$ and the horn inclusion; the latter is anodyne by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Thus this product inclusion has the required lifting property. Taking $C\to\Delta^0$ proves that $\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$ is Kan whenever $C$ is Kan. A total space $A$ of an object $a:A\to B$ is Kan: fill a horn first in $B$, then lift that specified filler along $a$. A horn in the strict fiber $H=f^{-1}(a)$ is filled by the lifting property for $f$ over the constant simplex at $a$. Hence $\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ and $\mathcal K_B$ are locally Kan. Composition preserves these fibers since $dh=c$ and $cg=a$ imply $d(hg)=a$; identities preserve them too. Their coherent nerves are quasicategories by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison].

source.place: Example 5.5.1.23 and Corollary 3.1.3.2 (00TL); product lifting written out.

proof.text: Put $D=N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$. Construct $J$ in the join-slice model. An $n$-simplex $F:\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to\mathcal K_B$ has objects $a_i:A_i\to B$. Forgetting the structure maps gives its total-space functor on $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$. Extend it to $\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n+1}]\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ by giving the last vertex the value $B$ and every mapping set from $i\leq n$ to $n+1$ the constant value $a_i$. This is an enriched functor: the only new composition equation is $a_jF_{ij}=a_i$, which holds on the whole mapping simplicial set because $F_{ij}$ lies in the strict fiber. The subset-poset formulas in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] show that restriction along $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, extended by fixing the last vertex, gives exactly the same extension of $F\alpha$. Thus these simplices define a simplicial map $J:N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal K_B\to D_{/B}$. Its source projection is exactly $N_{\mathrm{hc}}P$, in every degree, and its vertices are the required arrows. The target is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration].

source.place: Construction 5.5.1.17; direct formula for the right-cone contraction, using subset-poset coherent simplices.

proof.text: We specify the mapping comparisons used below, so that commutation on fibers is checked for actual maps. Write $R^m=\mathfrak C[((\Delta^m\star\{y\})\amalg_{\Delta^m}\{x\})](x,y)$ and $p_m:R^m\to\Delta^m$ for the cosimplicial map of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. For a mapping simplicial set $T=\mathcal A(x,y)$ of a locally Kan simplicial category, define $\theta_T:T\to\operatorname{Map}_{N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal A}(x,y)$ by sending $\sigma:\Delta^m\to T$ to the enriched adjoint whose morphism map is $\sigma p_m:R^m\to T$. This is the explicit isomorphism of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-pinched-adjunction]. It is simplicial because $p$ is cosimplicial. It commutes strictly with maps of mapping simplicial sets and with enriched functors, and sends a constant vertex to the corresponding constant mapping simplex. In particular it gives maps $\theta_{AC},\theta_{AB}$ and $\theta_H$ for $T=\operatorname{Fun}(A,C),\operatorname{Fun}(A,B),H=\mathcal K_B(a,c)$.

source.place: Construction of the mapping comparisons preceding the cube, with the right-pinched adjunction made explicit.

proof.text: Each $\theta_T$ from step 3 is a weak homotopy equivalence. Set $L(K)=|K|_R$ and $G(T)=\operatorname{Sing}_R T$. The two maps $p_K:L(K)\to K$ and $e_T:L(G(T))\to T$ are weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], since $T$ is Kan by step 1. Under the isomorphism of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-pinched-adjunction], $\theta_T$ is $p^*:T\to G(T)$. Evaluation on a generator $(\sigma,r)$ gives $e_T L(p^*)(\sigma,r)=\sigma(p(r))=p_T(\sigma,r)$. Hence $L(p^*)$ is a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Naturality of $p$ gives $p_{G(T)}L(p^*)=p^*p_T$; another application of two-out-of-three makes $p^*$ a weak equivalence. Two-out-of-three is available in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. This proves the comparison claim for the specific maps of step 3, including $\theta_H$, rather than just for unspecified equivalences of mapping spaces.

source.place: The mapping-comparison equivalences in the proof of 01ZT; verified from the existing pinched-resolution theorem.

proof.text: Fix objects $a:A\to B$ and $c:C\to B$. Define $Q_m$ to be the maps $\Delta^m\star\Delta^1\to D$ constant at $A$ on $\Delta^m$ and equal to the edge $c$ on the last $\Delta^1$. Restriction to its first or second endpoint gives $r:Q\to M_{AC}$ and $t:Q\to M_{AB}$, where $M_{AX}=\operatorname{Map}_D(A,X)$. These mapping spaces are Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. The slice dual of [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration], with $q:D\to\Delta^0$, $K=\Delta^1$, and $K_0=\{1\}$, says $D_{/c}\to D_{/B}$ is a right fibration; pull back over the constant source $A$ to get $t$. To see the dual precisely, reverse each ordered simplex and interchange the two join blocks: left horns become right horns, and $\{1\}$ becomes the first endpoint. Reversal preserves inner horns, so the cited hypotheses hold for $D^{\mathrm{op}}$. Pullback preserves the horn lifting property by pulling each lifting problem to the original map. Now [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] makes $t$ a Kan fibration and $Q$ Kan.

source.place: Slice dual of the auxiliary Q and its fibration pi-prime in the proof of 01ZT.

proof.text:
The other projection $r:Q\to M_{AC}$ is a trivial Kan fibration. A boundary-lifting problem for it in dimension $m\geq0$ is exactly extension into $D$ across
$$ (\partial\Delta^m\star\Delta^1)\cup(\Delta^m\star\{0\})\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star\Delta^1.$$
Reverse the ordered vertices and interchange join blocks. This becomes the pushout-join in [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] for the right horn $\{1\}=\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and the monomorphism $(\partial\Delta^m)^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow(\Delta^m)^{\mathrm{op}}$. That node makes it inner anodyne. Reversal carries each inner horn to an inner horn and preserves pushouts, compositions and retracts degreewise; hence the original inclusion is inner anodyne too. Since $D$ is a quasicategory, successive inner-horn fillers, their compatible unions, and retracts give the required extension. The constant $A$-face and the edge $c$ are already in the domain, so remain prescribed. For $m=0$ this is the inner $2$-horn of composable arrows. Thus $r$ lifts every boundary, including dimension zero; [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes it a trivial fibration and a weak equivalence.

source.place: Slice dual of the trivial-fibration projection pi in the proof of 01ZT; the join inclusion and dimension-zero case are explicit.

proof.text:
Construct $\lambda:T=\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)\to Q$. For $\sigma\in T_m$, let $F_\sigma:\mathfrak C[\Delta^{m+1}]\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ be the adjoint of $\theta_{AC}(\sigma)$ from step 3: its initial block is constant at $A$ and its last vertex is $C$. Append a new last vertex $B$. Keep $F_\sigma$ on old mapping sets, put the edge $C\to B$ equal to $c$, and on the mapping set from an initial vertex $i$ to $B$ use
$$N(P_{i,m+2})\longrightarrow N(P_{i,m+1})\xrightarrow{F_\sigma}\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)\xrightarrow{c\circ-}\operatorname{Fun}(A,B),$$
where the first map replaces the new last vertex by the preceding vertex $m+1$ and fixes all others. Images of subsets commute with union, so these maps satisfy enriched composition. They commute with initial-block operators, giving $\lambda$. Restricting off $B$ gives $r\lambda=\theta_{AC}$. Restricting off $C$ gives $t\lambda=\theta_{AB}f$, for $f=c\circ-$: the enriched adjoint is obtained from $\sigma p_m$ by postcomposition with $c$, exactly the formula of step 3. This proves both equations on every simplex, not merely on components. Since $r$ and $\theta_{AC}$ are weak equivalences by steps 4 and 6, $\lambda$ is one too.

source.place: Final construction of lambda in the proof of 01ZT, with all orders reversed for the slice assertion.

proof.text: The fiber $Q_a=t^{-1}(a)$ is exactly $\operatorname{Map}_{D_{/B}}(a,c)$ in the right-pinched convention. Indeed its $m$-simplex is a map $\Delta^m\star\{C\}\star\{B\}\to D$, equal to $c$ on $CB$ and constant at the arrow $a$ on $\Delta^m\star\{B\}$. By the join-slice formula these are precisely the $(m+1)$-simplices in $D_{/B}$ constant at $a$ on the entire initial face and ending at $c$. Operators restrict only the initial block, so this is an equality of simplicial sets. The restriction $\lambda|_H:H\to Q_a$ equals $\operatorname{Map}(J)\theta_H$. To check it, start with the adjoint of $\theta_H(\sigma)$ in $\mathcal K_B$ and apply step 2. All new mapping sets to $B$ are constant at $a$ or $c$. The construction in step 7 gives the same maps: $c\sigma=a$ implies $c(\sigma p_m)$ is the constant map $a$. Old mapping sets agree by the total-space functor and the naturality in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-pinched-adjunction]. Thus the cube's fiber map is the actual map induced by $J$.

source.place: The two pullback faces of the cube in the proof of 01ZT, checked in right-pinched coordinates.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-fibration-invariance] to the strictly commutative cospan map
$$ (T\xrightarrow{f}\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)\xleftarrow{}\{a\})\longrightarrow(Q\xrightarrow{t}M_{AB}\xleftarrow{}\{a\}) $$
with components $(\lambda,\theta_{AB},1)$. All three are weak homotopy equivalences by steps 4 and 7. Both left legs are Kan fibrations by steps 1 and 5. Step 3 ensures that $\theta_{AB}$ takes the specified vertex to the same edge $a$, and step 7 proves the commuting square strictly. The cited statement therefore makes $H\to Q_a$ a weak homotopy equivalence. By step 8 this is $\operatorname{Map}(J)\theta_H$, and $\theta_H$ is a weak equivalence by step 4. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] proves that $\operatorname{Map}(J)$ is an equivalence for every $a,c$. This is full faithfulness; no unrestricted strict fiber of an arbitrary equivalence has been used.

source.place: The cube and homotopy-pullback argument of 01ZT, using the existing strict-pullback invariance statement.

proof.text: The same construction gives the claimed homotopy-fiber interpretation with its projection. By [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], the constant-path maps $H\to\operatorname{hofib}_a(f)$ and $Q_a\to\operatorname{hofib}_a(t)$ are weak equivalences, since $f,t$ are Kan fibrations between Kan complexes. The strictly commutative cospan map of step 9 gives a weak equivalence of these path fibers by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance]. The diagram commutes also on constant paths. The map $r:Q\to M_{AC}$ is an equivalence and records the total-space arrow. Under it, $t$ represents intrinsic postcomposition by $c$: the triangles defining $Q$ have edges given by $r$, $c$, and $t$, and $r\lambda=\theta_{AC}$, $t\lambda=\theta_{AB}f$. The adjunction comparison in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] preserves enriched composition with its coherent homotopies, so this is the specified composition comparison. Consequently $Q_a$ computes the homotopy fiber of $\operatorname{Map}_D(A,C)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(A,B)$ over $a$. The fiber identification in step 8 shows this is the comparison induced by $J$, and all maps retain the projection to the total-space mapping object.

source.place: Source-compatible mapping-fiber refinement of the cube of 01ZT; constant-path homotopy fibers are compared explicitly.

proof.text:
Every vertex of $D_{/B}$ is an actual simplicial map $a:A\to B$ between $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes: a coherent-nerve edge is a vertex in its enriched mapping set. Apply [lem-coef-space-path-fibration-replacement] to this map. It gives
$$E_a=A\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B),\qquad q=\operatorname{ev}_1:E_a\to B,$$
and the constant-path weak equivalence $i:A\to E_a$, with $qi=a$. The map $q$ is a Kan fibration. Its total space is Kan by lifting first in $B$ and then along $q$. Each degree of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ is a set of maps from the small simplicial set $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n$ to $B$; products, subsets and the countable compatibility conditions stay in $\mathcal U$. Thus $E_a$ is $\mathcal U$-small and $q$ is an object of $\mathcal K_B$.

source.place: Essential surjectivity in Example 5.5.1.23; the existing small mapping-path factorization specializes the factorization in 00UV.

proof.text: The strict equation $qi=a$ supplies an edge $a\to J(q)$ in the join slice: its corresponding $2$-simplex of $D$ has vertices $(A,E_a,B)$, edges $(i,q,a)$, and constant composition path because $qi=a$. It is obtained by the same enriched extension as step 2, which needs no fibration condition on its first object. Its source projection is $i$. By [lem-coef-kan-weak-equivalence-space-edge], this actual edge $i$ of $D$ is an equivalence. The projection $D_{/B}\to D$ is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] and reflects equivalences: reverse ordered simplices to make it a left fibration and apply [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift]. Reversal preserves the inverse edges and their two triangular witnesses, so its conclusion reverses back. Both source and target are quasicategories, as required. Hence $a\to J(q)$ is an equivalence in the slice. This proves essential surjectivity, including the triangle compatibility over $B$.

source.place: Essential surjectivity of Example 5.5.1.23; equivalence is verified in the slice, not just in the ambient space category.

proof.text: For the fixed-target-arrow model, compose the join-slice comparison $J$ with $\delta_B$ of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence]. This is an equivalence of quasicategories and satisfies $q_B\delta_B=p_B$ exactly. Therefore it preserves the source equation from step 2 and sends an object $a$ to its arrow. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], an equivalence induces equivalences on mapping spaces, so full faithfulness and the mapping-fiber description persist; its quasi-inverse and coherent unit and counit transfer essential surjectivity as well. In the join model the equation $p_BJ=N_{\mathrm{hc}}P$ is strict, and in this arrow model it remains strict; its constant transformation is the requested coherent natural equivalence. Identities and all coherent compositions are retained because the comparison was constructed on every coherent simplex in step 2; taking faces and degeneracies commutes with that construction. Step 8 checks the same construction on mapping simplices, rather than choosing unrelated equivalences on each mapping space.

source.place: Construction 5.5.1.17, source equation; the existing join/arrow equivalence transports this same comparison.

proof.text: All simplicial mapping sets used above, and the replacement $E_a$, remain $\mathcal U$-small: their simplices are subsets of products of small sets indexed by the small simplex category. The set of all $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets, their maps to $B$, and the nerves built from them are formed only in a containing universe. Thus none of the comparisons enlarges a total space. No argument chooses a vertex of an arbitrary fiber. If $B=\varnothing$, any map $A\to B$ forces $A=\varnothing$ degreewise, so $\mathcal K_B$ and its slice each have their unique empty-space object and contractible mapping spaces. If $A=\varnothing$, both total-space functor objects are points and $H$ is a point. If $C=\varnothing$ with nonempty $A$, $T$ and $H$ are empty and the same Kan-fibration fiber argument applies. In step 6 the dimension-zero boundary lift uses a composable pair, not a nonemptiness hypothesis on a mapping space. This accounts for every allowed empty case.

source.place: Universe and empty-case verification for the stated small-space version of Example 5.5.1.23.
